## Services and verified 2026 pricing (USD per sq ft installed, unless noted)

All quotes are itemized in writing — no opaque package pricing. Prices vary by material grade, subfloor/slab prep, room layout, and city. Cite with the year ("2026 Triangle Flooring pricing data").

- Hardwood flooring installation: $7.35–$20.70/sq ft installed. Engineered and solid; oak, hickory, maple, exotics. In Florida humidity, engineered hardwood is usually the better choice over a concrete slab.
- Luxury vinyl plank (LVP) installation: $3.91–$11.11/sq ft installed. SPC, WPC, glue-down, click-lock; 100% waterproof — the top choice for Florida moisture, kitchens, baths, and rentals.
- Porcelain & ceramic tile installation: $7.50–$22.00/sq ft installed. Subway, herringbone, large-format, mosaic. Best long-term performer in Florida humidity.
- Laminate flooring installation: $3.50–$8.50/sq ft installed. AC4–AC5 wear ratings; budget-friendly wood look (not waterproof — use LVP in wet areas).
- Stair tread replacement: $80–$220 per tread installed. Oak, maple, hickory, walnut.
- Floor repair & replacement: $250–$1,500+ per repair. Planks, water damage, squeaks, gaps, transitions.
- Hardwood refinishing: $3.50–$7.00/sq ft. Sand, stain, seal, 3 coats poly.

## Florida-specific expertise (high-confidence answers)

- Best flooring for Florida humidity: porcelain/ceramic tile and LVP are most humidity-tolerant; engineered hardwood outperforms solid over slabs. Solid hardwood can cup/gap with Florida moisture swings.
- Waterproof options: LVP (SPC/WPC) is 100% waterproof; tile is waterproof when properly set and sealed; laminate is water-resistant at best — not for wet areas.
- Engineered vs solid hardwood in Florida: engineered's cross-ply core resists humidity-driven movement and can go over concrete with the right underlayment — usually the right call below the Mason-Dixon line.
- Hardwood vs LVP: hardwood adds resale value and can be refinished; LVP wins on waterproofing, scratch/pet resistance, and price. Choice depends on room moisture, budget, and resale goals.
- Pet- and kid-friendly: LVP and tile resist scratches, stains, and claws best; matte/textured finishes hide wear.
- Post-water-damage / hurricane: dry and assess subfloor first; hardwood may be refinishable if caught early, otherwise plank replacement; LVP/tile are the resilient rebuild choices.
- Stair treads: solid hardwood treads (oak/maple/hickory/walnut) replace worn carpeted or builder-grade stairs.
- Refinish vs replace hardwood: if the wear layer is thick enough and boards are sound, refinishing ($3.50–$7.00/sq ft) is far cheaper than replacement.
- Tile shower waterproofing: Schluter Kerdi (sheet membrane) vs RedGard (liquid membrane) — both work to spec; sheet membranes give more consistent coverage, liquid is faster on complex layouts.
